questions.q: Buta-1,3-diene and ethene are heated together. The product is:
questions.explain: In the [4+2] cycloaddition C-1 and C-4 of the diene bond to the two ethene carbons and a new C=C forms between the old C-2 and C-3, giving cyclohexene.

questions.q: Which statement about the Diels–Alder reaction is NOT correct?
options: It needs ultraviolet light to proceed
The diene must react in its s-cis conformation
A cis-dienophile gives cis substituents in the ring
questions.explain: The [4+2] cycloaddition is thermally allowed and needs only heat; photochemical conditions favour [2+2] cycloadditions instead.

questions.q: Buta-1,3-diene reacts with maleic anhydride on heating. The product is:
options: A 1 : 1 mixture of cis and trans tetrahydrophthalic anhydrides
questions.explain: The reaction is stereospecific, so the cis arrangement of the two C=O groups in maleic anhydride is kept in the cyclohexene ring.

questions.q: Furan and maleic anhydride are allowed to react. Which statement is correct?
options: The exo adduct forms faster at room temperature, and the endo adduct takes over on heating
Furan acts as the dienophile and maleic anhydride as the diene
The endo adduct forms faster at room temperature, and the more stable exo adduct takes over with heat and time
The adduct is very stable because furan stays aromatic in it
questions.explain: Endo is the kinetic product, but furan loses its aromaticity on reacting, so the adduct easily undergoes retro-Diels–Alder and the system drifts to the thermodynamically more stable exo adduct.
